title: Your First Decade Is a Position
subtitle: A field guide for building financial agency from 2026 to 2036.
audience: A college graduate entering the 2026 economy and learning to navigate money, work, AI, and ownership.

authors.name: Codex
authors.role: research, editorial development, interaction design, and implementation

thesis: The first decade of a career is not mainly a portfolio-selection problem. It is a sequence for building margin, compounding systems, portable skill, durable ownership, and the capacity to help useful institutions last.

three_machines.name: Margin
three_machines.definition: Income not already promised to essential commitments.

three_machines.name: Compounding
three_machines.definition: Small financial and professional systems that keep working after payday.

three_machines.name: Ownership
three_machines.definition: A claim on value that can outlive one job.

order_of_operations: Know monthly take-home pay, essential monthly cost, required debt payments, and reachable cash.
Keep required payments and the insurance floor intact.
Build a starter cash buffer sized to the reader's actual risks.
Inspect expensive debt by balance, interest rate, minimum payment, and consequence.
Read employer contributions, vesting, eligibility, and fees before acting.
Automate a survivable contribution and understand long-horizon risk, diversification, and cost.

decade_map.proof: A system that runs on a bad week
Public proof that travels without a job title
A small institution with a reason to exist
